description: Validates edge policy rules for rate limit definitions, CORS header safety, WAF rule validity, geo-restriction format correctness, and contract-level policy auditability

rules.description: edge-policy-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare name and a non-empty rules array

Every edge rule must declare a rateLimit with requestsPerSecond or requestsPerMinute. Rules without rate limits allow unlimited traffic through the edge, removing the primary DDoS protection layer. Set skipRateLimitRequirement: true for internal-only routes

When cors is configured, allowedOrigins must be a non-empty array. allowedOrigins=['*'] combined with allowCredentials=true is a security misconfiguration — browsers reject credential requests to wildcard origins. allowedMethods must use only recognised HTTP verbs. Gate skipped when no cors block is present

Every WAF rule must have an id (for auditability), a match expression (to define what triggers the rule), and a valid action. waf.mode must be 'detection' or 'prevention'. Gate skipped when no waf block is present

All country codes in geoRestrictions.allowlist and denylist must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (two uppercase letters). Invalid codes are silently ignored by most CDN/edge providers — the restriction appears configured but never applies. allowlist and denylist cannot both be specified

constraints.exclusive: allowlist and denylist cannot both be declared — choose one mode

rules.description: edge-policy-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers. Placeholder rate limits or WAF rules will either have no effect or block all traffic unexpectedly
Every rule must be identifiable with a name or match field for audit log correlation. requestsPerSecond must be a positive number when declared. Policy-level name is required for auditability

constraints.rule-identity: every rule must have name or match
